The improved bottom-line (where STLA reported a loss of €0.01 versus a loss of €0.04 last year) helped offset larger than expected free cash outflow and a conservative outlook for FY26.
Wall Street applauded the mixed results as the company’s efforts to trim costs are showing progress. But analysts are less convinced that Stellantis

“Stellantis reported a mixed set of Q3/2026 numbers with FCF outflow that was bigger than expected but also a sizeable beat on earnings in North America. That said, the challenges remain present, and more than one quarter’s beat is needed to sustainably turn around the business,” said Deutsche Bank analyst Christoph Laskawi, adding that as the environment for the auto industry becomes more challenging, the cost-saving measures are crucial in the coming years.
“We don’t believe product will be enough,” Citi Research analyst Harald Hendriksen says, “and the key question remains how STLA will improve North America and Europe’s AOI.”
“Until this recovery gains momentum in reported earnings, we think the shares will likely remain under pressure,” Hendriksen says, reiterating his Neutral/High Risk outlook on Stellantis.

Faced with the continued fallout from its failed EV strategy and subsequent write-downs, cash drain and tariff-related pressures, as well as intense competition from cheaper Chinese vehicles in Europe, Stellantis

“Fixing Europe is harder than launching a hit pickup, because the pressure here is structural: too many brands, thin pricing power, rising costs, and relentless competition,” AutoNext reported back in July.
And the latest results showed the challenges in Europe persisted for another quarter with negative AOI attributed to a difficult pricing environment that outpaced cost savings and higher volumes.
